subject: Nimble call recap — lab hypotheses + A/B test plan
messages:
From: Evan Torres <evan.torres@nimble.ai>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: post-demo traces and latency questions

Thanks for the demo this morning, Dylan — good conversation. Two quick asks from our infra/ops team after the call:

1) We captured traces from our internal prod workload vs what we saw on the demo. Attaching a trimmed trace (nimble_trace_072908.jsonl) showing a few 95/99 spikes during multi-user microbursts. Can you confirm whether Redwood's KV-cache or prefix-sharing would reduce the p95 spikes we see here?

2) We'd like to validate p95/p99 across two scenarios: short-context chat (max 256 tokens, 99% of requests) and long-context summarization (up to 2048 tokens, heavy KV reuse). We want a simple A/B: Redwood default config vs Redwood with aggressive batching + 8-bit quantized model.

Our ops team also asked for an apples-to-apples latency/cost comparison vs their current hyperscaler endpoint (they're on a managed LLM endpoint from HyperCloud). Key metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (steady-state and during 1-min microbursts), and cost per 1M tokens.

Can you share a proposed lab plan and an ETA for run results? We can provide a small sample corpus and workload generator.

—Evan

Attachments: nimble_trace_072908.jsonl (4.1 MB, trimmed)

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Evan Torres <evan.torres@nimble.ai>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: post-demo traces and latency questions

Evan — thanks for the trace and for laying out the exact asks. High-level reply + proposed next steps below. I copied Marissa and Jordan so we can coordinate lab capacity and timelines.

Quick answers:
- KV/prefix caching: yes — in the short-chat scenario (256 tokens) prefix/KV reuse will materially reduce p95 in steady-state when requests share recent context. Microburst behavior depends on batching window; we'll test both conservative and aggressive batching.
- Quantization: 8-bit will reduce per-token cost and typically improves throughput for token generation-heavy workloads; we need to confirm any small delta in p99 under microbursts (sometimes quantized kernels slightly increase tail under heavy concurrency).

Proposed plan (we can run this in our dedicated test harness in ~48–72 hours if you provide the corpus + workload generator):
A) Baseline: run Nimble workload against their HyperCloud endpoint (their side will provide) and Redwood hosted default config. Capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost estimates.
B) Redwood A/B: Default vs (Aggressive batching + KV enabled + 8-bit quant). For each: short-context (256) and long-context (2048) workloads. 10 minute steady-state, then 5x1min microburst windows (simulate bursts at 5x baseline concurrency).
C) Region & routing probe: run Redwood in us-west and us-east to measure cross-region variance and smart-route fallback latency.
D) Deliverable: single spreadsheet with metric breakdown (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens), sample traces, and suggested config knobs to match HyperCloud SLA.

Owners / deadlines:
- Redwood test lead: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.com) — set up runs, produce spreadsheet (ETA: 72 hours)
- Internal engineering triage: Jordan Blake (jordan.blake@redwood.com) — validate kernel/quant configs and confirm any fallback model variants
- Sales owner: me (Dylan) — coordinate logistics and commercial framing

Attachments we will produce: redwood_vs_hyper_testplan_0729.xlsx (test matrix + config), run logs, and aggregated spreadsheet.

I'll schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to confirm corpus + access. Sound good?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0149

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimble call recap — lab hypotheses + A/B test plan

Folks — summary of the lab hypothesis matrix and immediate asks for Eng/Infra (putting this in ticket-friendly language):

Hypotheses:
1) For short-context chat (256 tokens): enabling prefix/KV sharing + 50–100ms batching window will reduce p95 by ~20–35% vs Redwood default.
2) For long-context summarization (2k tokens): KV reuse reduces tokens/sec latency but may increase cumulative latency per request; expect tokens/sec uplift under quantized kernels for GPU types with optimized 8-bit paths.
3) Under 1-min microbursts, aggressive batching can lower mean latency but may increase p99 tail — need to measure tradeoff.

Test matrix (high level):
- Baseline Redwood default (no quant, conservative batching)
- Redwood + KV + 50ms batching
- Redwood + KV + 200ms batching + 8-bit quant
- Hyperscaler (HyperCloud managed endpoint) baseline

Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 (generation-only), tokens/sec (steady-state), tokens/sec during microbursts, GPU utilization, and cost-projection per 1M tokens (including infra + model license).

Immediate infra asks (Neha / Eng):
- Neha: can you queue a Redwood dedicated harness run for July 11 00:00–06:00 UTC? We need two GPU nodes (same family) for comparative runs and a captive traffic generator.
- Jordan: please sanity-check the quantization kernel flags against Aurora and Cobalt families — call out any kernel-fallbacks that might skew p99.

Outputs to attach to the HubSpot record: full test spreadsheet, run traces, and a short executive one-pager recommending config (we'll draft).

Marissa Cole
Sr. Eng Manager, Performance
Redwood Inference

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nimble call recap — lab hypotheses + A/B test plan

Acked. I'll reserve the test harness window and spin up two identical Cobalt nodes for the comparative runs on July 11 (UTC window Marissa requested). Quick notes:

- I'll enable detailed tracing and KV cache logging; expect 1.2GB of trace artifacts per 10-minute steady-state run.
- Quant flags: will run both q8h and q4f where q8h is the primary quant target (we'll note any fallback to fp16 kernels).
- For cost calc we'll include GPU hours, model weights egress, and memory overhead from KV caches.

I'll upload the testplan spreadsheet as redwood_vs_hyper_testplan_0729.xlsx and drop the Drive link (added to related_links).

-Neha
